findings.label: Probable error
findings.confidence: Moderate: Buddha may be implied by a conventional reading of the teachings/treatises pair, but the present source does not name that possessor.
findings.problem: “The Buddha’s teachings” adds a specifically named speaker while the proposed བཀའ་ entry and the surrounding teacher category say only teachings. Neither N-B012 nor N-B013 records the supplied possessor.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove Buddha’s and retain teachings; alternatively explicitly disclose this possessor interpretation rather than treating it as established.

findings.label: Confirmed error
findings.problem: “Having trained ..., the primordial knowing ... will blaze forth” grammatically makes primordial knowing the trainer. The practice is undertaken by the implicit practitioner; the blazing forth follows it.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a finite when-clause with the practitioner as subject; retain the disclosed provisional as-relation and all established terms.

findings.label: Confirmed error
findings.problem: “Has never been experienced to arise” uses a nonstandard complement of experienced. It makes an otherwise intelligible observation needlessly difficult.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the complement to as arising; the experiential force and denial are retained.
